text:
maria: Proposal: operatorless ephemeral connector — dataplane uses short-lived outbound tunnels from customer VPC to our regional relay instead of requiring VPC peering or private endpoints. Quick thread to capture tradeoffs: latency, egress IP preservation, cert rotation, ops surface. Thoughts?
kevin: sounds interesting. main win is zero customer infra changes, right? no peering, no VPCE creation.
anika: yes, policy-wise it's easier. but we trade off predictable egress IPs and might add ~1-2 RTT for tunnel setup if connections are short-lived.
lee: agree with @anika. curious about how long-lived the tunnels are. if we keep them warm with heartbeats it looks more like a managed sidecar.
maria: idea was ephemeral: connect-on-demand, keep-alive window configurable (default 60s). cheaper for customers who dont want long-lived endpoints.
sam: how do we handle egress IP preservation for customers who need allowlisting? Many customers require static IPs.
anmika: (typo) -> anika: For allowlist customers we can offer a gateway-mode where regional relays advertise a small stable egress pool, but that requires them to allow our egress CIDRs. still less work than peering.
jordana: what about TLS/key management? operatorless means we need to bootstrap identity without running agents.
maria: plan: short-lived client certs minted via control-plane-issued JWT -> STS-like exchange. Flow: customer creates an onboarding token in console, paste into login CLI -> agentless connector does TLS mutual auth with short certs.
kevin: sounds similar to token-exchange pattern we've used before. Audit trail needs to be clear — who created token, scopes, revocation window.
ops-bot: reminder: if we mint short certs we need to store revocation list or adjust cert TTLs. Ops prefers short TTLs to avoid CRL complexity. :warning:
lee: another ops point: NAT and path MTU. Tunneling increases packet size; need to validate PMTU across common CSPs.
maria: +1. add a CI smoke test that spins up a small EC2 in a new VPC and establishes the flow, verify PMTU, DNS, health-checks.
sam: what about latency-sensitive workloads like chat inference? extra hop to regional relay adds tail latency. Can we route to the closest regional relay and then to Dedicated pools?
anika: yes, smart routing can pick lowest-latency relay per customer. But for sub-50ms needs, we probably recommend VPCE/dedicated peering.
jordana: rollout idea: start with preview for non-prod customers, telemetry on tunnel setup time, keepalive churn, error rates. Expose a metric: connector_handshake_ms and connector_conn_per_min.
maria: good. also need fallback semantics: if ephemeral connector fails, app can optionally fallback to public hosted API (with warning) or block. Document in SDK.
kevin: SDK change ok. also add new error code so callers can detect connector vs control-plane failures.
lee: curious about cost model: relays will take more connections and NATs. need to estimate egress bandwidth + connection churn. Might need autoscaling hooks at relay layer.
maria: noted. put cost estimate exercise on infra backlog: estimate connections/sec at 1M dailies -> warm windows, NAT throughput.
ops-bot: action item created: INFRA-ephemeral-connector-cost-estimate (link: https://go/infra/INFRA-ephemeral-connector-cost-estimate) :white_check_mark:
jordana: security: ephemeral approach reduces customer config errors but increases our blast radius. Tight scoping of tokens + observability required.
anika: add network policy: default deny on relay egress to non-customer clusters. only allow downstream to pinned model pool endpoints.
maria: decision checklist for RFC: 1) Security flow (token+cert) 2) Telemetry + rollback 3) Performance SLOs and canary plan 4) Cost model 5) Docs + SDK errors 6) Fallback semantics.
kevin: think we should also add a hybrid operator option: customers can either use ephemeral operatorless flow OR install a small connector binary that pins to a static ENI for static egress. Gives most flexibility.
sam: hybrid seems pragmatic. allowlist customers pick connector binary + ENI, others use operatorless.
lee: ops question: how will we support customers behind strict firewall policies that only allow specific outbound ports? we need to support 443 and maybe 7844? better to only use 443.
maria: design decision: use TLS over 443 only. keep protocol multiplexed over ALPN. No custom ports.
jordana: final note: testing matrix: non-prod canary (10 customers), perf bench (p95 handshake < 250ms), security audit, cost pilot. Then 6-week gradual ramp.
maria: thanks all — I'll spin up an RFC follow-up doc with the checklist and link here. @kevin @jordana please review when I post. :+1:
